title: DAR assures P600-M quick response fund amid El Niño threat
summary: The Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) said it has a P600-million quick response fund (QRF) ready to cushion agrarian reform beneficiaries against the looming effects of Super El Niño.

blocks.text: The Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) said it has a P600-million quick response fund (QRF) ready to cushion agrarian reform beneficiaries against the looming effects of Super El Niño.
Budget sponsor Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan said this during the Senate plenary deliberations into the proposed P16.121 billion budget of the DAR for fiscal year 2027.

“Dati walang quick response fund ang DAR. Naglaan tayo this year ng P600 million in anticipation of the impact of El Niño. Kaya meron silang quick response fund para matutukan ‘yung magiging impact ng El Niño lalo na sa ating mga magsasaka that form part of the agrarian reform beneficiaries and the communities,” he said.

(Previously, the DAR did not have a quick response fund. This year, we allocated P600 million in anticipation of the impact of El Niño. This provides them with a quick response fund to address the effects of El Niño, particularly for our farmers, that form part of the agrarian reform beneficiaries and the communities.)
Pangilinan gave the update after Senator Bong Go asked about the preparations of DAR to mitigate the expected effects of El Niño on agrarian reform beneficiaries (ARBs).

“With the threat of El Niño, we are concerned about its potential adverse effects on our agricultural sector, particularly on our agrarian reform beneficiaries whose livelihood heavily depends on farming,” Go said.

“Hindi po sapat na mabigyan lang ng sariling lupa ang ating mga magsasaka. Kailangan ding tiyakin natin na mayroon silang sapat na suporta lalo na sa panahon ng kalamidad at matinding tagtuyot,” he added.
(It’s not enough to simply provide our farmers with their own land. We must also ensure that they have sufficient support, especially during times of calamity and severe drought.)

According to Pangilinan, the DAR is implementing solar-powered irrigation projects in partnership with the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) to ensure a more reliable water supply amid the El Niño.
He said the agency is also endorsing the use of El Niño-resilient crops and is offering climate-resilient farm productivity support to help increase yields and improve household incomes of the ARBs.
The senator said these projects are expected to benefit 579 communities, 734 agrarian reform beneficiary organizations (ARBOs), and 26,900 ARBs.

Of the P949 million allocated for the two programs, Pangilinan said P219 million is proposed for the Sustainable Livelihood Support for Disaster Areas, while P730 million would go to the Major Crop Farm Productivity Enhancement.
He said both programs aim to provide extension services, farm inputs, farm machinery, among others, to assist agrarian reform beneficiaries. — BAP, GMA News
